title: Restore deployability of artifact-ticket sandbox backend
description:
## Problem

The additive artifact-ticket backend fails Amplify sandbox type validation because environment configuration is applied through an interface that does not expose that supported operation. This blocks the early application-authentication and transfer acceptance gate.

## Expected behavior

Given the additive artifact-ticket backend is present
When the existing Amplify sandbox is synthesized and deployed
Then backend type validation succeeds
And the ticket resolver receives its required table and bucket configuration
And Cognito login plus a real signed artifact round trip can be tested before consumer migrations proceed.

## Scope

Repair the supported Amplify/CDK resource integration, add a regression contract, redeploy the existing sandbox, and record sanitized acceptance evidence. Do not add direct-storage, API-key, AWS-SSO, or silent fallback behavior.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Kickoff: coordinator /root is working in /Users/ryan.porter/Projects/Plexus-aws-login-free-sandbox-fix on branch codex/aws-login-free-sandbox-deploy-fix, based on 815943c53. Owned scope: reproduce the Amplify type-validation failure, add a behavior-first regression contract, repair the supported backend resource integration, redeploy the existing sandbox, and run Cognito plus signed-transfer acceptance. Dependency boundary: Wave 2 consumer branches remain unmerged and the evaluation consumer lane remains paused until this gate passes.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Milestone: early sandbox acceptance found two deployment defects before any Wave 2 merge. First, backend type validation rejected calling addEnvironment on the exposed IFunction; the repair uses the supported Amplify function resource method. Second, CloudFormation detected a data/function nested-stack cycle; the resolver is now assigned to the supported data resource group. Regression specifications failed for each defect before implementation and now pass. Focused contract: 3 passed. Generated schema contract is current and its check passes. Next: deploy once to the existing named sandbox, then exercise Cognito login and signed HTTPS transfer.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text:
Sandbox acceptance found a second pre-login packaging defect after the infrastructure deployment passed: a clean locked Poetry installation could not start the `plexus` CLI because `click` is imported by the command framework but is not declared as a direct project dependency. This blocks the observable login scenario before the hosted authorization page opens.

Next: add a behavior-first packaging regression, declare the runtime dependency explicitly, rerun the clean CLI smoke test, and then resume Cognito login, identity, refresh, GraphQL, and signed artifact-transfer acceptance with AWS credential environment variables removed.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Behavior-first CLI startup coverage now passes after two minimal fixes: `click` is an explicit core runtime dependency, and the installed entrypoint dispatches `login`, `whoami`, and `logout` before importing the legacy scoring command graph. The observable `plexus login --help` startup dropped from tens of seconds in the full environment to 0.57 seconds. Focused auth tests are green except the deliberate occupied-port test while the real sandbox login listener is currently using that port.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text:
Live Cognito acceptance passed `plexus whoami` and an authenticated AppSync collection query with AWS credential variables and the API key removed. The first `GraphQLArtifactStore` write then failed closed before ticket issuance because its mutation declares `$requests` as `[ArtifactTransferRequest!]!`, while the deployed schema requires `[ArtifactTransferRequestInput!]!`. This unit-test blind spot allowed the returned object type to be confused with the mutation input type.

Next: add an exact mutation-variable contract assertion, correct the operation, rerun focused tests, then repeat the same credential-free signed PUT/GET round trip.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text:
Sandbox acceptance is green with all local AWS credential/profile variables and the API key removed.

Evidence:
- Real hosted Cognito authorization-code login completed and stored the refresh credential in the OS keychain.
- `plexus whoami` returned the sandbox test identity.
- A Cognito-authenticated AppSync collection query succeeded.
- An explicitly expired access-token cache refreshed from the keychain without user or AWS-login intervention.
- `GraphQLArtifactStore` completed a signed HTTPS PUT/GET round trip; 54 downloaded bytes matched the declared SHA-256.
- Local `boto3.client("s3")` was forced to raise during the round trip and was never invoked.
- `plexus logout` revoked and removed the application session, and the temporary sandbox user was deleted.

Acceptance exposed and fixed four defects before the storage-migration lanes merge: unsupported Amplify function environment mutation, a cross-stack dependency cycle, the Python mutation's wrong GraphQL input type, and an unsigned duplicate checksum header on signed PUTs. It also added explicit CLI framework packaging, lightweight auth-command dispatch, and a numeric-loopback callback server that does not wait on reverse DNS.
